content: {"summary":"fraud-scorer-02 was OOMKilled roughly every 11 minutes after a node rotation placed it on a 32‑core node; the pod ran 32 gunicorn workers because WEB_CONCURRENCY was unset, exceeding its 3 GiB memory limit despite normal redis latency and ordinary tracemalloc traces.","likely_cause":"The default worker count (WEB_CONCURRENCY) derived from the node’s CPU count caused twice as many gunicorn workers (32) to run, consuming more memory than the pod limit and triggering OOM kills.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The node rotation moved fraud‑scorer‑02 onto a 32‑core node, where the OOM loop began.","evidence_ids":["INC-0163#1"],"quote":"node rotation drains the node under fraud-scorer-02; the replacement pod lands on one of the 32-core nodes"},{"text":"WEB_CONCURRENCY was not set, so gunicorn started one worker per CPU, i.e., 32 workers.","evidence_ids":["INC-0163#1"],"quote":"WEB_CONCURRENCY is not set in the Deployment, so the entrypoint starts one gunicorn worker per CPU it can see: 32"},{"text":"Each worker uses ~150 MiB; with ~20 workers memory hits the 3 GiB limit, causing OOM after about 11 minutes.","evidence_ids":["INC-0163#2"],"quote":"The kill came once about 20 workers had warmed up ... each start lasted about 11 minutes"},{"text":"The usual memory‑growth cause (feature‑cache growth when redis‑features is slow) was not present because redis latency was normal.","evidence_ids":["RB-006#0","INC-0163#1"],"quote":"feature cache grows without bound when redis-features is slow"},{"text":"Worker count is tied to node core count via GOMAXPROCS, not container limits, a known pattern for over‑commitment.","evidence_ids":["RB-002#2"],"quote":"sets GOMAXPROCS to the node's core count, not the container limit"}],"next_checks":["Verify that WEB_CONCURRENCY is explicitly set to a safe value (e.g., 16) in the fraud‑scorer deployment","Confirm current GOMAXPROCS and worker count on pods running on 32‑core nodes","Monitor per‑worker memory usage after the change to ensure no hidden leaks","Audit other services that derive concurrency from node CPU count for similar risks"]}
